decision.analysis: Round 1 results establish a clear hierarchy: resnet18 (0.9789 acc) > residual_cnn (0.9718 acc) > compact_transformer (0.9455 acc). The compact_transformer underperformed significantly, likely due to its very small hidden dimension (48) which is well below the 128-256 range recommended by the CCT literature. The residual_cnn and resnet18 both used hidden=32, depth=3, suggesting the CNN family is well-suited to this 28×28 pathology task. For round 2, I will: (1) substantially upgrade the compact_transformer to hidden=128, depth=3, mlp_ratio=4 to give it a fair shot at the 1-4M parameter budget; (2) push the residual_cnn deeper (depth=5, hidden=64) with additional augmentation to see if more capacity + data diversity closes the gap to resnet18; (3) refine the resnet18 configuration with class weighting (to address the 1.63× imbalance), slightly higher label smoothing, a different geometric augmentation (rotate90), and a larger batch size (256) for more stable gradient estimates. All three candidates use standardize normalization, AdamW, cosine scheduling, and conservative weight decay (1e-4) consistent with the research guidance.

candidates.rationale: Round 1's compact_transformer used hidden=48, far below the 128-256 embedding dimension recommended by CCT evidence (arXiv 2104.05704). With hidden=128, depth=3, mlp_ratio=4 (FFN dim=512), and 4 heads (32-dim per head), the model lands in the 1.5-3M parameter range appropriate for 90K samples. Patch size 4 on 28x28 yields 7x7=49 tokens, preserving spatial detail. Switching from attention pooling to cls pooling reduces variance in the readout. LR lowered to 3e-4 for the larger model. Conservative augmentation (hflip, rotate180) preserves tissue orientation cues. This is the first fair test of the compact_transformer hypothesis.

Round 1's residual_cnn (hidden=32, depth=3) achieved 0.9718, close to resnet18's 0.9789. Doubling hidden to 64 and increasing depth to 5 (within the 4-6 block recommendation) gives the residual architecture more capacity to model complex histological patterns. Dropout raised to 0.15 to regularize the deeper network. Adding rotate180 and brightness augmentations (3 total, within the max-3 limit) increases effective training diversity without destroying tissue-orientation cues. LR kept at 1e-3 which worked well in round 1. This tests whether a well-tuned residual CNN can match or exceed resnet18 at lower parameter cost.

Resnet18 led round 1 at 0.9789. This candidate refines it: (1) class_weighting=true directly addresses the 1.63x imbalance (classes range 7886-12885 samples) by up-weighting minority classes in the loss; (2) label_smoothing raised to 0.1 for additional regularization of confident predictions; (3) rotate90 augmentation adds a different geometric invariance than the hflip/vflip used in round 1, potentially helping with orientation-agnostic features; (4) batch_size=256 provides more stable gradient estimates (350 steps/epoch vs 700); (5) hidden=48 and depth=4 give slightly more capacity than round 1's 32/3; (6) LR lowered to 3e-4 for the larger effective model. This tests whether targeted loss-level and augmentation changes can push past 0.98.
